pre_mortem: Warren: Pittsburgh could lead without giving him enough carries, particularly if Dowdle takes a larger share or Cleveland improves its run defense. The 4.54 defensive YPC does not guarantee Warren's efficiency, and his recent aggregate could conceal uneven workloads. Judkins: Cleveland could outperform its underdog expectation, sustain drives and expand his workload; receiving production or one explosive run could also defeat the under despite limited carries. Both are script-dependent, and Cleveland taking control is the strongest common counter-case.
slip_story: Both leans belong to one conditional story: Pittsburgh leads and runs while Cleveland's rushing opportunities diminish. Neither survives the Cleveland-controls-the-game flip reliably. No 3–4-leg main slip is built because only two players have supported hypotheses; adding another leg would manufacture an edge.
